The challenge you face is that bullets are done in HTML and the HTML tag for bullets is single-spaced. Adding the appropriate HTML requires editing the source of the message and that requires adding an addon for that feature, so the appropriate tag can be added. I recommend you not attempt that. If it's important, then get this addon: ThunderbirdHTMLEdit at https://betterbird.eu/addons/ and after inserting the bullets, edit the initial tag (I assume <ol> if numbered), with this tag: <ol style="line-height: 2;">

That creates double-spacing. Use 1.5 for line and a half.

content:
re :Is a primary password required? Generally no.

However, if you share your computer with other people AND you allow them access to your computer User Account (you gave them your User Account password) AND you do not want them to have access to stored passwords then you could create a Primary Password which must be unique and never the same as a mail account passwords. But it will not stop people from seeing emails or have access to your profiles. It just stops people seeing Thunderbirds stored passwords. If there is an attempt to remove the Primary Password, then it will also delete any stored passwords because you want them protecting.

Check you do not have software which can remove certain files like passwords. If you have stored passwords being erased, then check to see if you have any Cleanup software that has access to your profile folders. Cleanup software can erase password, session, temp and cache files. Cleanup software like CCleaner or WiseCleaner or even your Anti-Virus may have the ability.

If you use any of the above and you want to keep using them, I would advise you access the program eg: Anti-Virus and set up an exception to not scan your thunderbird profile folder. If you downloaded Thunderbird from the official Thunderbird webpage then the 'Thunderbird' folder that contains all profiles is here: eg: C://Users/username/Appdata/Roaming/Thunderbird
